name: Grocery Store Near Me in Singapore: How to Find Supermarkets and Food Shopping Options
content:
Typing "grocery store near me" into Google is usually the first step when you've just moved into a new flat, you're visiting a different neighbourhood, or your usual supermarket has run out of something you need. Singapore is unusually well-served for grocery shopping — most HDB estates have at least one supermarket, a wet market, and several minimarts within walking distance — but knowing how to search effectively and what to expect from each option makes the process faster and cheaper.

This guide explains the practical ways residents find nearby grocery stores in Singapore, the main supermarket chains you'll encounter, and how to combine physical shopping with online grocery delivery for the best results.

Key takeaways

  • Searching "grocery store near me" on Google Maps or a mapping app is the fastest way to locate nearby options, since your device's location — not this website — determines what's actually closest to you.
  • Singapore's grocery landscape includes major supermarket chains (NTUC FairPrice, Sheng Siong, Giant, Cold Storage), wet markets, and convenience stores, each suited to different shopping needs.
  • Most HDB neighbourhoods have a supermarket within a 5–10 minute walk, often on the ground floor of a nearby block or in the neighbourhood's commercial centre.
  • Online grocery shopping (FairPrice On, RedMart, Sheng Siong's online store) is a practical alternative when you can't get to a physical store or want goods delivered.
  • Comparing a few nearby options for price and freshness — rather than defaulting to the first result — can meaningfully reduce your monthly grocery bill.

How "near me" searches actually work

When you search "grocery store near me," your search engine or maps app uses your device's GPS or Wi-Fi location to show results physically closest to you at that moment. This website cannot detect your live location, so instead of guessing, the most reliable approach is:

  1. Open Google Maps or Apple Maps and search "grocery store" or "supermarket" — your current location is used automatically.
  2. Check store locator pages on major supermarket websites (FairPrice, Sheng Siong, Giant, Cold Storage all have official store locators with full addresses and opening hours).
  3. Ask your building or estate's directory — HDB estates often list nearby amenities including supermarkets and wet markets on notice boards or town council websites.
  4. Use ride-hailing or delivery apps like Grab, foodpanda, or Deliveroo, which show nearby grocery and supermarket partners based on your location.

The main types of grocery stores you'll find in Singapore

Supermarkets (chain stores)

These are the default choice for most households doing a full weekly or monthly shop.

Chain What it's known for
NTUC FairPrice Singapore's largest grocery retailer, widest network of branches, competitive pricing, FairPrice On for online orders
Sheng Siong Known for value pricing on fresh produce and meat, strong presence in HDB heartland estates
Giant Larger-format stores, often in malls or standalone locations, though the chain has reduced its store count in recent years
Cold Storage Positioned slightly more premium, wider imported and specialty product range

Wet markets

Many neighbourhoods still have a traditional wet market, often paired with a hawker centre. Wet markets are typically the best source for fresh produce, live seafood, and meat at competitive prices, though they usually close earlier in the day (often by early afternoon) and accept mostly cash, though cashless payment is increasingly available.

Minimarts and convenience stores

7-Eleven, Cheers, and independent minimarts are useful for quick top-ups — a missing ingredient, drinks, or snacks — but are generally more expensive per item than a full supermarket run.

Online grocery delivery

If getting to a physical grocery store near me isn't convenient, online options include:

  • FairPrice On — NTUC FairPrice's online delivery and click-and-collect service
  • RedMart (Lazada) — a long-established online grocery platform in Singapore
  • Sheng Siong online store — for delivery within their service areas
  • Amazon Fresh Singapore — grocery delivery integrated with Amazon Singapore

Practical tips for finding the right grocery store near you

  • Check opening hours before heading out. Sheng Siong outlets often open early and some run extended hours; FairPrice branches vary by location, with some open 24 hours.
  • Compare more than one option if you have the choice. Sheng Siong and FairPrice frequently trade places on which is cheaper depending on the specific item — Sheng Siong tends to have an edge on fresh produce, while FairPrice's overall basket cost is sometimes marginally lower.
  • Don't overlook the wet market for fresh items. If your estate has one, it's often the most economical source for vegetables, fish, and meat, especially early in the morning.
  • Use store locators, not just search results. Supermarket chains publish full lists of branch addresses and hours on their own websites — these are more reliable than generic map pins for confirming a store is still operating at that address.

Household essentials vs fresh groceries: shop smart

Most residents split their shopping between:

  • Fresh groceries (produce, meat, fish, dairy, bread) — best bought fresh and often cheaper at wet markets or during in-store promotions.
  • Household essentials (cleaning products, toiletries, pantry staples) — these keep well, so it's worth stocking up during sales, and price differences between chains tend to be smaller here than for fresh items.

Frequently asked questions

How do I find the nearest grocery store to my address? Use Google Maps or Apple Maps and search "grocery store" or "supermarket" with location services enabled — this shows options physically nearest to you, sorted by distance.

Is FairPrice or Sheng Siong cheaper? It depends on the specific items. Independent price comparisons have found FairPrice slightly cheaper overall in some baskets, while Sheng Siong is often more competitive on fresh produce and meat. The best approach is to compare prices on the items you buy most.

Can I get groceries delivered instead of visiting a store? Yes. FairPrice On, RedMart, and Sheng Siong's online store all offer delivery within Singapore, typically with a delivery fee unless you meet a minimum order value.

Are wet markets still relevant for grocery shopping in Singapore? Yes, especially for fresh produce, seafood, and meat. Many residents combine a wet market visit for fresh items with a supermarket trip for packaged goods and household essentials.

What if there's no big supermarket near my flat? Check for minimarts, convenience stores, or wet markets nearby for immediate needs, and consider online grocery delivery for a fuller shop if the nearest full supermarket is inconvenient to reach.

Final practical takeaway

The fastest way to find a grocery store near me in Singapore is to let your phone's location services do the work through Google Maps or a supermarket's own store locator, rather than relying on generic search results. Once you know your nearby options, compare based on what you actually buy — fresh produce may be cheaper at a wet market, while household essentials are often similarly priced across the major chains.
